newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Tuesday on speculative buying triggered by short-covering at the opening session after continued losses over the past few trading days, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,040 yuan ($2,777) per tonne, rising 320 yuan. It opened at 22,670 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 22,660 and a high of 23,050.
April rose 330 yuan to 23,350, May 270 to 23,160, June 240 to 23,100, August 320 to 23,050, September 300 to 23,000, and October 80 to 22,880 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 56,800 tonnes from 52,730 tonnes.
Copper opened mostly up on short-covering, followed by speculative buying which strengthened the gains for the rest of the session.
"Speculative buying dominated today's trading because they believed copper was not likely to fall sharply in the next few days under the support of higher physical copper prices," one trader said.
Spot copper prices are around 23,100 yuan per tonne in Shanghai area.
But some traders said Tuesday's buying was for quick profits and it was not likely to keep this trend in the short term.
"The general long-term outlook for copper futures was not optimistic, so it will meet resistance at high levels in the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium followed copper's trend. April rose 50 yuan to 15,450, May 120 to 15,600, June 150 to 15,800 and July 100 to 15,900 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 1,760 tonnes from 1,140 tonne.
